DS Analysis: Allen turns 31 this offseason, but he's playing some of the most efficient football of his career and still piling up rushing scores. He's beaten his expected fantasy output every season we have data for, which keeps him the safest dynasty QB1 on the board.

Burrow is healthy and posting the best TD rate of his career this year, a reminder that few passers can match his efficiency. The injury history is the only knock, and it's why he sits a notch below the top two.

Williams went from 31.7 points below expectation as a rookie to above it in Year 2, and his efficiency has taken another step this season. At 25 with real rushing ability, he's a locked-in dynasty QB1 for the next decade.

Maye made a massive Year 2 leap, jumping from 6.7 to 8.9 yards per attempt, and he's stayed efficient this season even with more turnovers. He's 24, he runs and he's still on his rookie deal, which makes him one of the best long-term holds at the position.

Lawrence beat his expected output in 2025 after three straight years below it, and his passing efficiency has climbed again this season. At 27 with four years left on his deal, he's settled in as a legit dynasty QB1.
Mahomes' 2023-24 dip looked like the start of a decline, but he's bounced back with his most efficient play in years. He's 31 and signed through 2034, so the dynasty window is still wide open.

Purdy is having the most efficient season of his career, and he's never posted fewer than 7.6 yards per attempt in any year. At 27 and signed long term in a QB-friendly system, he's about as stable as dynasty QB1s get.

Daniels' 891-yard rookie rushing season set an absurd bar, and injuries have kept him from matching that pace since. He's still only 26 with a top-five ceiling, though the hits he takes as a runner are worth watching.
Love is having the best fantasy season of his career, building on three straight years of beating his expected output. He doesn't add much as a runner, but at 28 he's a steady dynasty QB1.

Gibbs has topped 21 PPR points per game in back-to-back seasons, and his role has grown into a true workhorse load this year. He's 24, signed long term and consistently beats his expected output, which makes him the dynasty RB1.
Goff has beaten his expected fantasy output in four straight seasons in Detroit. At 32 with zero rushing value, though, his dynasty appeal is mostly for teams trying to win now.
Robinson has been a top-tier workhorse since Year 2, handling a 63% carry share with 100+ targets in 2025. He's only 24 and has one of the safest three-down roles in the league.

Stroud has bounced back this season after two muted years, looking much more like the QB who averaged 8.2 yards per attempt as a rookie. He's only 25, so he's a strong buy if anyone in your league is still discounting him.

Herbert's TD rate has been stuck between 3.6% and 5.1% since 2022, and this season has been the worst of his career. He's 28 and still capable of a bounce-back, but he's barely hanging on as a dynasty QB1.
Dak has been one of the most consistent fantasy QBs of the last decade, and he's in the middle of another strong season. At 33 the window is shrinking, but he's a high-end QB2 for contenders.

Chase has been a top-tier fantasy WR every year of his career, highlighted by a 103.6-points-over-expectation 2024 season. At 26 and signed through 2030, there's no reason to move off him as a dynasty WR1.

Nix's legs have carried his fantasy value, and his efficiency through the air has dipped even further this season. He's 26 with his rookie deal nearing its end, so he's a QB2 who needs to grow as a passer.
Walker finally got a true lead role after leaving Seattle, where he shared work for most of his career. At 26 with two years left on his deal, he's in his prime and set up as a high-end RB1.

Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his rookie efficiency has been bumpy so far. Nothing about his long-term outlook has changed, though: he's 21 with elite athleticism and a clear path to a featured role in Arizona.
Darnold posted back-to-back seasons of 7.9+ yards per attempt, but the turnovers have resurfaced this year. He's 29, so view him as a QB2 with streaky upside.
Smith-Njigba went from a 1.83 YPRR to 3.72 in 2025 with a 36.8% target share, and he's somehow been even better this season. He's 24, locked up through 2032 and the top dynasty WR in the game.

Lamar's thumb injury is a short-term concern, but he's still the most explosive rushing QB in fantasy when he's on the field. His rushing volume did dip in 2025, and that's the trend to watch as he turns 30.
Lamb had a down 2025 by his standards, but he's rebounded to near-elite form this year and has posted 2.3+ YPRR in each of the last four seasons. At 27, he remains a locked-in dynasty WR1.

Nabers commanded a 35.7% target share as a rookie before missing most of 2025, and he's still been a target magnet in his return. He's 23 with elite talent, so the QB play and offense around him are the only things holding back his fantasy output.
Young has climbed out of a brutal rookie year and is having his best fantasy season yet. He's 25 and trending the right way, but he still needs to prove he's more than a high-end QB2.

St. Brown has posted 2.4+ YPRR and a 26%+ target share in four straight seasons, which is about as consistent as it gets. He's 27 and doesn't rely on speed, so he should age gracefully as a dynasty WR1.

Jefferson was 42.5 points below expectation in 2025, and Minnesota's QB issues have kept dragging him down this year. He's 27 with a 28%+ target share in every season, so he's a buy-low dynasty WR1 if you believe the situation gets fixed.

Cook has turned himself into a full-time back, with his carry share climbing every season and 55+ points over expectation in each of the last two years. He's 27 and signed through 2030, so he's an RB1 for at least a couple more seasons.

London has earned a 28%+ target share in three of his four seasons and keeps producing through shaky QB play, though the TDs have dried up this year. He's 25 and signed through 2031, so he's a strong dynasty WR1/WR2.
Flowers broke out in 2025 with 1,211 yards and 2.62 YPRR, and he's signed in Baltimore through 2032. At 26 he's a steady dynasty WR1/WR2 with room for more.

McBride has posted a 27%+ target share in three straight seasons, which is elite even among WRs, though his efficiency has dipped a bit this year. He's 27 and signed through 2030, so he's a locked-in TE1 for several more years.
Bowers put up 112 catches as a rookie and has been even more efficient this season. He's 23 with a WR-like skill set, making him the clear dynasty TE1.
Mendoza is a 23-year-old rookie with a long runway in Las Vegas. The sample is too small to judge, but his age and starting opportunity make him a QB2 hold with QB1 upside.

Jeanty has had the volume but not the efficiency through two seasons, though Las Vegas has gotten him more involved as a receiver this year. He's 22 with three-down ability, so the blocking around him is the main thing holding him back.

Taylor's 2025 was a reminder of his ceiling (77% carry share, 71 points over expectation), but his efficiency has dipped this year. He's nearing 28 and doesn't catch many passes, so the dynasty window is shorter than his ranking suggests.

Nacua is dealing with knee and toe injuries, but his 3.79 YPRR and 36.6% TPRR in 2025 were absurd. He's 25 and one of the best target earners in football, so his expiring contract is the only real dynasty question.
Mayfield's 2024 was a career year (7.2% TD rate), but he's regressed in each season since and has really struggled this year. At 31 he's a QB2/QB3 with limited dynasty value.

Golden had a quiet rookie year on a limited route share, but he's broken out this season as a full-time player in Green Bay. He's 23 with legit speed, making him one of the biggest risers at the position.

McMillan topped 1,000 yards as a rookie with a 25.7% target share, and his production has ticked up in Year 2. He's 23 with prototypical size, so it should keep climbing as Carolina's passing game improves.
Loveland beat his expected output by 19.4 points as a rookie, but his efficiency has cooled in Year 2. He's 22 and still has a big role in Chicago, making him a long-term TE1.
Olave has been a consistent 2.0+ YPRR producer with a 29% target share in 2025. Concussions are the lingering concern, but at 26 and signed through 2031, he's a solid dynasty WR2.
Collins has been one of the most efficient WRs in football, with 2.4+ YPRR in three of the last four seasons. He's nearly 28 and has missed time in most years, but he's a strong WR2 when healthy.

Higgins has beaten his expected output in every season we have data for, and he's having one of his best years. He's nearly 28 and signed through 2029, so he's a win-now WR2 with a few good years left.

Achane is recovering from a torn ACL, which clouds his short-term outlook. Before the injury he was one of the most explosive backs in football with 85+ targets in back-to-back seasons, and at 25 he has time to rebuild that value.
Likely spent years as an efficient part-timer in Baltimore, and he's broken out as New York's starter this season. He's 26 and signed through 2029, making him a legit TE1.

Pickens broke out in Dallas with 1,429 yards and 48.9 points over expectation in 2025. He's 25 with his contract up, so his next deal and landing spot will determine whether he stays a dynasty WR1/WR2.
Warren earned a 21.5% target share as a rookie, but his efficiency has slipped further this year. He's 24 with three-down usage, so the volume should keep him in the TE1 mix while he develops.
LaPorta has beaten his expected output by 27+ points in each of his first three seasons. He's 25 but heading into free agency, so his next contract and landing spot are the big dynasty questions.
Fannin earned a 25.5% TPRR as a rookie and beat his expected output, which is rare for a 21-year-old TE. He's 22 and set up as Cleveland's top receiving option for years.

McCaffrey proved he's still elite with a 129-target 2025, and he's kept producing at a high level this year. He's 30 with an expiring deal, so he's a must-start for contenders and a sell-high candidate for rebuilders.

Hall has been a consistent producer, but his efficiency has slowly slipped since his 2023 breakout (17.1 PPR points per game). He's still 25 with real receiving chops, keeping him on the RB1/RB2 border.
Judkins has gotten plenty of volume through two seasons, but he's been well below expectation both years. He's 23 and Cleveland is committed to him, but he needs the offense around him to improve.
Kraft beat expectation by 45+ points in both 2024 and 2025, but his production has cooled this season. He's 26 and signed through 2031, so he's still a strong dynasty TE1.

Washington broke out in 2025 on a part-time route share and has earned a full-time role this year. He's 24 with his contract expiring, so his next deal will determine whether he's a WR2 or WR3 long term.

Hampton showed RB1 upside as a rookie before injuries cut his season short, but he's shared more work than expected this year. He's 23 with a three-down profile, so he's a buy-low RB2 for patient managers.

Irving bounced back nicely this season after an injury-shortened 2025, looking more like the efficient back he was as a rookie. He's 24 with a strong receiving profile, making him a solid RB2 with RB1 weeks.
Kincaid has been ultra-efficient on a part-time role (3.02 YPRR in 2025), but Buffalo has never given him a full-time route share. He's 27, so he's a TE1 when healthy with a capped ceiling.

Brown has been a reliable volume back with 85+ targets in 2025, but his efficiency has slipped below expectation this year. He's 26 with his contract up after this season, so his next landing spot will shape his long-term value.
Tate is a 21-year-old rookie who's earned a full-time role in Tennessee right away. His youth and route-running give him a high ceiling, making him a top dynasty stash at the position.

Hurts is dealing with a blood clot in his calf, which adds uncertainty to his outlook. His rushing TDs also slid from 13-15 per year to eight in 2025, so the elite fantasy ceiling isn't as safe as it once was.
Coleman is a 23-year-old rookie who's produced above his workload in Denver's backfield. He has the size and receiving skills to stick as a lead back, making him a high-upside RB2 in dynasty.
Price is a 23-year-old rookie who's been stuck in a committee in Seattle and hasn't been efficient early. His receiving ability gives him a path to more work, but he's a stash for now.
Watson has been an elite per-route producer when healthy, and he's finally putting it together for a career year. He's 27 and signed through 2031, but his injury history keeps him in the WR2 range.
Tuten barely played as a rookie but has broken out this season as Jacksonville's lead back. He's 23 with home-run speed, making him a strong RB2 with upside.
Penix has yet to string together a full healthy season, and his TD rate has hovered between 2.9% and 3.3%. He's 26 and still on his rookie deal, but he's a QB2/QB3 until he shows more.
Tyson is a 22-year-old rookie who's still working his way into a full-time role in New Orleans. He has the talent to be a WR1 down the road, but he's a stash for now.

Wilson has been stuck in bad offenses his whole career, which shows up in his below-expectation numbers. He's 26 and still earns a ton of targets, so he's a buy-low candidate if New York ever fixes its QB situation.
Concepcion is a 22-year-old rookie who's earned a role in Cleveland. He's a versatile slot weapon with upside, but the QB situation limits him for now.

Lemon is a 22-year-old rookie who's earned a full-time role in Philadelphia, though the efficiency hasn't come yet. He's a slot-heavy prospect with a long dynasty runway, making him a WR3 with upside.
Williams has been a volume king for three seasons, though the Rams have started to mix in more help. He's 26 with two years left on his deal, so he's a solid RB2 with a shrinking ceiling.
Hubbard has bounced between workhorse and backup roles, and this season he's back to being a true lead back. He's 27, so enjoy the production, but his inconsistent track record makes him an RB2.
Sadiq is a 21-year-old rookie with rare athleticism for the position. He's still working into a full-time role, but he has the profile of a future dynasty TE1.

Burden was a hyper-efficient part-timer as a rookie (2.79 YPRR on a 42% route share) and has since earned more snaps. He's 22 with a skill set built for PPR leagues, making him a strong WR2 with upside.

Rice has been one of the most efficient slot WRs in football when available, but his role has shrunk this year. He's 26 with his contract up, so his next landing spot and availability are the big questions.
Shough has gotten more volume this year, but the efficiency still isn't there. He's 27, which shortens his dynasty runway, so treat him as a QB2.

Ward was 47.5 points below expectation as a rookie, and he's improved this year without fully turning the corner. He's still 24 with the arm talent that made him a No. 1 overall pick, so he's a QB2 with upside.
Smith has topped 1,000 yards in three of the last four seasons and has beaten his expected output every year we have data for. He's 28, so he's best as a steady WR2 for contenders.
Williams has topped 1,000 yards in back-to-back seasons with 46+ points over expectation in each. He's 25 and signed through 2030, making him a strong WR2 in Detroit.

Dart is working back from a meniscus injury, but his rookie year showed exactly why he belongs in the QB1 tier. Nine rushing TDs in 14 games gives him a weekly floor few young QBs can match, and he's only 23.
Odunze has been below expectation in each of his first two seasons, and his target share has dropped this year. He's 24 with big-play ability, but he's sliding toward WR4 territory.
Boston is a 22-year-old rookie with a big frame and a full-time role in Cleveland. He's a WR3 with upside if the passing game around him improves.
Willis flashed big efficiency in limited Green Bay action and finally got his shot to start. The abdomen injury slows him down, and at 27 he looks more like a QB2 bridge than a long-term answer.
McConkey's rookie year (2.56 YPRR, 54.7 points over expectation) was outstanding, but his efficiency fell in 2025 and his role has shrunk this season. He's 25, so he's a buy-low WR3 with upside.
Pitts finally delivered a full season in 2025 (88 catches, 15.2 points over expectation), but he's regressed this year. He's 26 and signed through 2029, making him a volatile back-end TE1.
Kittle has beaten his expected output by 40+ points in four straight seasons and is still producing at a high level. He's 33, though, so he's a win-now TE1 rather than a long-term hold.
Egbuka was 26.1 points below expectation as a rookie, and his efficiency has slipped further this season. He's 24 with good route-running skills, but he needs a turnaround to stay a WR3.
Williams is a 22-year-old rookie who's already working into Washington's rotation. He's a WR4/WR5 stash with a chance to grow into more.
Waddle has had an up-and-down career, and his first season in Denver has been rough. He's 28 with a history of efficient production (2.41 YPRR in 2025), making him a WR3/WR4.
Cooper is a 22-year-old rookie who's flashed big-play ability in a part-time role. As his route share grows, he has a path to WR3 value in New York.
Bernard is a 22-year-old rookie who stepped into a real role in Pittsburgh. He's more of a high-floor possession type than a ceiling play, making him a WR4 with room to grow.
Moore's efficiency cratered in his final Chicago season (1.26 YPRR), but he's looked much better in Buffalo. He's 29 with three years left on his deal, making him a WR3/WR4.
Brown has been one of the most efficient WRs in football for years, but he's 29 and has gotten off to a slow start in New England. He's a win-now WR3 with declining dynasty value.
Corum has been efficient whenever he's gotten work, and his role has grown this season. He's 26 and still behind Kyren Williams, so he's a handcuff with real standalone value.
Mayer never topped 6 PPR points per game in his first three seasons. He's 25 and has a bigger role now, but he's a TE2 with limited upside playing next to Bowers.
Lane is a 22-year-old rookie in a part-time role in Baltimore. He's a taxi-squad stash with a big catch radius.
Henry turns 33 soon and the efficiency is finally starting to slip from his 2024 peak (5.9 yards per carry). He's a win-now RB2 at best with one year left on his deal.

Jacobs has beaten his expected output in both full seasons in Green Bay, but he's missed time this year. He's nearly 29 with one year left on his deal, so he's a win-now piece and a fading dynasty asset.
Raridon is a 22-year-old rookie working into a role in New England. He's a stash with upside.
Stowers is a 23-year-old rookie with a WR-like skill set who's still waiting for a real role in Philadelphia. He's a high-upside stash with a clear path once Goedert moves on.
Wilson is dealing with a neck injury, and while he's seen big volume this year, the efficiency hasn't followed. He's 26 and signed through 2030 after his 1,006-yard 2025, making him a WR3.

Skattebo flashed as a rookie with a 25% target rate before injury ended his season, and he's carried a bigger load this year without the same efficiency. He's 24 with an every-down style, though durability remains the question.
Metcalf has never quite matched his physical tools with elite efficiency, and he's had a tough year in Pittsburgh. He's nearly 29 and signed through 2030, making him a WR3/WR4 with a fading ceiling.
Monangai earned real snaps as a rookie in Chicago and has run well when given work. He's 24 and a strong handcuff behind Swift with standalone value.
Johnson is a 23-year-old rookie who's already shown a knack for producing above his workload. His receiving skills give him a path to a bigger role in Kansas City.
Freiermuth has quietly beaten expectation by 19+ points in each of the last two seasons. He's 28 and a reliable TE2 with occasional TE1 weeks.
Barkley's 2024 season was one of the best in recent memory, but his efficiency dropped off in 2025 and his role has shrunk this year. He's 30 next season, so he's a win-now asset only.
Strange has steadily grown his role in Jacksonville and beat expectation by 17.9 points in 2025. He's 25 and signed through 2030, making him a solid TE2.
Coker has carved out a steady role in Carolina, though his 1.4 to 1.8 YPRR hasn't hinted at a breakout. He's 25 and signed through 2030, so he's a useful WR4 with bye-week value.
Williams revived his career in Dallas with a 62% carry share after two rough years in Denver. He's 26 and signed through 2029, making him a solid RB2 despite limited receiving upside.
Hockenson looked like he was fading in 2025 (1.15 YPRR), but he's bounced back this season. He's 29 with an expiring deal, making him a short-term TE2.
Schultz has been a volume-based producer in Houston with limited efficiency. He's 30, making him a short-term TE2.
Addison scored 9+ TDs in each of his first two seasons before falling off in 2025 (1.52 YPRR). He's 24, so he's a buy-low WR4 who needs a bigger role to bounce back.
Andrews' 2024 season (11 TDs, 60.9 points over expectation) was his last great year, and he fell off in 2025 (1.30 YPRR). He's 31, so he's a TD-dependent TE2.
Black is a 25-year-old rookie stuck in a committee behind McCaffrey. He's a handcuff and stash until San Francisco's backfield opens up.
Evans is 33 but has looked rejuvenated in San Francisco after an injury-plagued 2025. He's a win-now WR3 with very little long-term value.
Okonkwo has been a steady but unspectacular producer, hovering around expectation for most of his career. He's 27 and now in Washington, making him a TE2.

Thomas had a monster rookie year (2.55 YPRR, 50.4 points over expectation) but fell off in 2025, and his role has shrunk even further this season. He's 24, so he's a buy-low lottery ticket if he can recapture that form.
Johnston scored eight TDs in both 2024 and 2025, but his role has dried up this year. He's 25 with his deal ending soon, making him a WR5 whose next home matters.
Henry beat his expected output by 19.5 points in 2025 and has been a steady producer in New England. He's 31, making him a short-term TE2.
Johnson broke out in 2025 with 77 catches and 15.6 points over expectation. He's 30, so he's a short-term TE2 in New Orleans.
McLaurin is dealing with a knee injury and turned 31 this season. He was excellent in 2024 (59.4 points over expectation), but he's a short-term WR3/WR4 now.
Brazzell is a 23-year-old rookie dealing with a knee injury. He's a taxi-squad stash until he gets healthy.
Swift has been a reliable RB2 for years, beating expectation by 19.8 points in 2025. He's nearly 28 and signed through 2030, but the receiving work that made him special has faded.
Adams is dealing with a hamstring injury, and at 33 with an expiring deal, the dynasty window is closing fast. He still scored 14 TDs in 2025, so he's a win-now WR3.
Kelce is 37 with an expiring deal, but he's still been efficient this year. He's a win-now TE2 with retirement always looming.
Douglas is a 23-year-old rookie who's earned a meaningful role in Miami. He wins downfield and is a WR4 with upside if the target share keeps climbing.
Goedert scored 11 TDs in 2025 and beat expectation by 45.6 points. He's 31 with an expiring deal, making him a win-now TE2.
Ferguson is dealing with an ankle injury and has been a part-time player through two seasons. He's 23 with upside, but he's a stash for now.
Flournoy has been efficient in a part-time role (1.82 YPRR in 2025) and has worked his way into more snaps. He's 27, so his ceiling is a WR5 with spot-start value.
Stafford turned back the clock in 2025 with a 7.7% TD rate, but he's come back down to earth this year and is about to turn 39. He's a pure win-now piece with retirement always on the horizon.
Etienne has swung between above and below expectation every year, and his move to New Orleans has started slowly. He's nearly 28, making him a volatile RB3.
Barner beat expectation by 26 points in 2025, but he's struggled this year with an extremely low aDOT. He's 24, making him a TE3.
Pearsall is dealing with a PCL injury and hasn't been able to stay healthy through his first two seasons. He's 26, so he's running out of time to stick as a starter.
Dell flashed big upside as a rookie (25.2 points over expectation), but injuries have derailed his career since. He's 27 with an expiring deal, making him a deep bench piece.
Stribling is a 23-year-old rookie dealing with an ankle injury. He's a taxi-squad stash until he gets on the field.
Gadsden had a nice rookie year (664 yards, 1.79 YPRR), but his role has shrunk this season. He's 23, so he's a buy-low TE2/TE3 stash.
Helm flashed as a rookie with a 23.7% TPRR on a part-time role. He's 24 and a TE3 with upside.
Allen is a powerful 22-year-old who's carved out a bigger role in New York. His receiving work is limited, which caps his ceiling, but he's a young RB3 with upside.
Bell is a 22-year-old rookie with a limited role in Miami. He's a taxi-squad stash.
Pierce is dealing with a heel injury but topped 1,000 yards in 2025 with a 19.0 aDOT. He's 26 and a boom-bust WR4 in best-ball formats.
Warren has taken over as Pittsburgh's lead back and has been efficient doing it. He's 28 with one year left on his deal, so he's a solid RB2 for contenders.
Bryant has been a part-time player in Denver through two seasons. He's 23, so he's still a reasonable deep stash.
Otton has a full-time route share but has been below expectation in each of the last two seasons, and he's been even worse this year. He's 27 and a TE3 at best.
Ferguson peaked with 82 catches in 2025, but his receiving role has shrunk this year. He's 27 and signed through 2030, making him a TE2/TE3.
Hunter is being used almost exclusively on defense right now, which kills his fantasy value. He's 23 with rare talent, so he's a hold only if you believe Jacksonville will move him back to offense.
Delp is a 23-year-old rookie who's barely played in New Orleans. He has the athleticism to develop, but he's a taxi-squad stash for now.

Charbonnet has been efficient in a committee role, beating his expected output by 13+ points in each of the last two seasons. He's 25 with his contract expiring, and a move to a lead role could unlock RB2 value.
Sarratt is a 23-year-old rookie who has barely played in Baltimore. He's a taxi-squad stash.
Stevenson had a nice bounce-back 2025 (35.6 points over expectation) as the receiving complement in New England. He's nearly 29, so he's a short-term RB3.
Croskey-Merritt has been an efficient runner in Washington's backfield as a mid-round pick. He's 25 and doesn't catch many passes, so he's an RB3/RB4.
Hurst is a 22-year-old rookie with a part-time role in Tampa Bay. He's a downfield threat and a decent taxi-squad stash.
Gordon has grown into a bigger role in Year 2 but hasn't been efficient. He's 22 and has the size to be a goal-line weapon, making him a decent RB4 stash.
Pittman is dealing with a foot injury in his first season in Pittsburgh. He's 29 and has always been more volume than efficiency (1.5 to 2.1 YPRR), making him a WR4.
Worthy's elite speed hasn't translated into efficiency yet (1.36 YPRR in 2025). He's 23 and still has upside, but he's a WR4/WR5 until the production shows up.
Ayomanor was well below expectation as a rookie (38.5 points short). He's 23 with some size and athleticism, but he's a WR5 until his efficiency improves.
Klare is a 23-year-old rookie stuck behind a crowded Rams TE room. He's a taxi-squad hold.
Dike has been a part-time player through his first two seasons in Tennessee. He's 24 and a deep stash.
Mason has been an efficient backup throughout his career but hasn't sustained a lead role. He's 27 with his contract expiring, making him an RB4.
Meyers has been a reliable possession WR his whole career, but he turned 30 this year. He's depth for contenders and little more.
Mitchell has been well below expectation in every season of his career (49 points short in 2024). He's 24 with big-play ability, but the production hasn't come.
Henderson is battling an illness, and his role has shrunk this year after an efficient rookie season (5.1 yards per carry). He's 24 with talent, making him a buy-low RB3.
Harrison was below expectation in both of his Arizona seasons and has struggled after moving to Houston. He's 24 with the pedigree to bounce back, but he's a speculative WR4/WR5 until it happens.
Dulcich has bounced around the league but showed a pulse in Miami (2.54 YPRR in 2025). He's 26 with an expiring deal, making him a TE3.
Washington is a 23-year-old rookie behind Jeanty in Las Vegas. He's a deep stash with handcuff value only.
Higgins is recovering from a torn ACL after a promising rookie year (12.2 points over expectation). He's 23, which makes him a worthwhile buy-low stash.
Branch is a 22-year-old rookie being used as a gadget piece in Atlanta. He's a speculative taxi-squad hold.
Johnson has been a below-expectation producer in New York through three seasons. He's 25 and a TE3.
Coleman has been a part-time player through his first two seasons in Buffalo, never topping 8.6 PPR points per game. He's 23 and a WR5.
Fields is a 23-year-old rookie with a big frame and a starting role in New York. He's a WR4/WR5 stash whose value depends on how the offense develops around him.
Boerkircher is a 25-year-old rookie with a part-time role in Jacksonville. He's older for a rookie, which limits his upside.
Shakir has been a steady PPR producer from Buffalo's slot, beating expectation by 25+ points in back-to-back seasons. He's 26 and signed through 2030, making him a WR4.
Engram is 32 with an expiring deal and has been below expectation in each of the last two seasons. His dynasty value is gone.
Sutton has been a reliable producer for years, but he's 31 and his production has fallen off a cliff this season. He's a short-term WR5 at best.
Tucker has hovered around expectation as a part-time producer in Las Vegas. He's 25 with his deal up, making him a WR5.
Harris has been a part-time player through his first two seasons in Los Angeles. He's 24 and a WR5 with some size.
Arroyo is dealing with a shoulder injury and was below expectation as a rookie. He's 23 and a deep stash.
